module.cors.checks: Checks the cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) policy: reflected arbitrary origin, “*” and credentials.
module.cors.fix:
Find where CORS is defined: the application, the framework, the web server, the API gateway or the CDN (search for `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` in each layer). Several layers may add the header: fix the one that reflects the origin.
Replace the reflection of the `Origin` header with an explicit allow-list of full origins (`https://app.example.com`), compared exactly: never a "starts with" or "ends with" test on the domain. Send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` only if the received origin is in the list, and nothing otherwise (see the snippet).
Reject the `null` origin (local or sandboxed documents): it must never be in the list.
Send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` only for origins in the allow-list, and only if the API needs it (cookies, HTTP authentication). Never combine it with `*`: browsers reject that combination. Otherwise, remove this header.
When the value depends on the origin, add `Vary: Origin` so that a cache or a CDN does not serve the response for one origin to another. Also limit `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` to what is strictly needed.
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` remains acceptable for public resources without authentication (fonts, open data, libraries). Make sure no session or user-specific data is served on those paths.
If the origin was reflected with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, a third-party site could read your users' authenticated responses: review the access logs for requests carrying a foreign `Origin` header, and invalidate sessions or renew exposed tokens if needed.
Check: `curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://evil.example.net' https://example.com/ | grep -i access-control` must print nothing; with an allowed origin, the same command must return exactly that origin. Then run the scan again.
module.cors.title: CORS
module.cors.why: Accepting any origin together with credentials lets any website read the data of logged-in users.
